cards.b: c.1400-1600. Revival of Greek and Roman ideas; perspective, anatomy, realism.
A system for showing depth where parallel lines meet at a vanishing point (Brunelleschi, Alberti).
Soft, smoky blending of tones without hard outlines; Leonardo da Vinci.
Strong contrast between light and dark in a picture.
Very dark shadows with a strong spotlight. Caravaggio.
c.1600-1750. Drama, movement, emotion. Caravaggio, Rembrandt, Velazquez.
By Velazquez (1656), in the Prado, Madrid.
c.1760-1830. Order and clarity inspired by ancient Greece and Rome; Jacques-Louis David.
c.1800-1850. Emotion, imagination and the power of nature: Turner, Delacroix, Goya, Friedrich.
Goya, painted 1814; French soldiers shoot Madrid citizens; in the Prado.
c.1840-1880. Ordinary working people painted honestly: Courbet, Millet.
1870s-1880s France. Broken brushstrokes, bright colour, light, painting outdoors.
Tiny dots of pure colour that mix in the eye; Seurat, La Grande Jatte.
c.1885-1905. Van Gogh, Cezanne, Seurat, Gauguin: personal expression beyond Impressionism.

short.q: State two features of the Renaissance.
short.model: Artists used linear perspective to show depth and studied anatomy for realistic bodies, reviving ideas from ancient Greece and Rome.
Realism showed ordinary people and everyday life honestly, while Romanticism focused on emotion, imagination and the power of nature.

short.q: How could you use Caravaggio in a still-life project?
short.model: Light fruit with one lamp in a dark box and draw in charcoal with white chalk to get strong contrast and drama.
He built on Impressionist colour but moved to personal, expressive thick paint and emotional colour rather than recording light.

short.q: Name two Impressionist painters and one feature of one.
short.model: Monet and Renoir; Monet used broken brushstrokes to show light on water.
